title: Identifying Endogenous Proximal Proteins via Biotinylation and Antibody Recognition
author: Rega, Pardo, et al.
materials: Goat anti-mouse IgG Alexa Fluor Plus 488

steps.title: Culture cells to confluency
steps.instruction: Grow cells in 15‑cm plates to ~80 % confluency in the recommended cell‑culture medium; plan for at least 1 mg total protein lysate (minimum) and use 10 mL total buffer volume per plate unless otherwise noted.

steps.title: Fix cells
steps.instruction: Fix cells as described in step 2 of the original protocol (details not provided here).

steps.title: Permeabilize cells
steps.instruction: Permeabilize the cells as described in step 3 of the original protocol.

steps.title: Inactivate endogenous peroxidases
steps.instruction: Inactivate endogenous peroxidases as described in step 4 of the original protocol.

steps.title: Apply primary and HRP‑conjugated antibodies
steps.instruction: Use antibody recognition to direct HRP to the protein of interest as described in step 13 (include primary antibody incubation and HRP‑conjugated secondary antibody).

steps.title: Perform proximity biotinylation
steps.instruction: Carry out the proximity‑labeling reaction as described in step 14, adding 2 mL of biotinylation buffer per 15‑cm plate.

steps.title: Quench biotinylation reaction
steps.instruction: Immediately add quenching buffer to stop the biotinylation reaction; work quickly and time the reaction accurately (critical step).

steps.title: Lyse cells and collect lysate
steps.instruction: Prepare cell lysate as described in step 15, using 150 µL of lysis buffer per 15‑cm plate; lysates may be stored at –80 °C.

steps.title: Enrich biotinylated proteins with streptavidin beads
steps.instruction: Enrich biotinylated proteins using streptavidin magnetic Dynabeads as described in step 16, adding 100 µL Dynabeads for each 1 mg of lysate (optimize as needed).

steps.title: Optional western‑blot validation
steps.instruction: Take aliquots of the bead‑bound material for western‑blot validation to confirm enrichment before mass‑spectrometry analysis.

steps.title: On‑bead reduction, alkylation and trypsin digestion
steps.instruction: Process the bead‑bound proteins for MS:

substeps.instruction: Resuspend beads in 100 µL of 100 mM TEAB.
Add 4 µL reducing buffer; incubate 10 min at 15‑25 °C while shaking at 1000 g.
Add 6 µL alkylating buffer; incubate 45 min at 15‑25 °C in the dark while shaking at 1000 g.
Add 10 µL of 0.2 mg/mL trypsin (2 µg); incubate 12‑18 h at 37 °C while shaking at 1000 g.
Add an additional 2 µg trypsin; incubate 3 h at 37 °C while shaking at 1000 g.
Place tubes on a magnetic rack, pellet beads, and transfer the supernatant to a new tube.

steps.title: Acidify peptide eluate
steps.instruction: Acidify the peptide solution by adding formic acid to a final concentration of 1 % (v/v).

steps.title: Optional TMT labeling
steps.instruction: If quantitative comparison is desired, label the peptides with isobaric mass tags (e.g., TMT) after acidification.

steps.title: Peptide cleanup
steps.instruction: Clean up peptides to remove contaminants using either Cellulose Acetate Filter Spin Cups or C18 tips according to the manufacturers’ instructions.

steps.title: Dry peptides
steps.instruction: Dry the cleaned peptide samples in a vacuum concentrator.

steps.title: LC‑MS/MS acquisition
steps.instruction: Run the dried peptides on an Orbitrap Fusion Lumos coupled to an Ultimate 3000 RSLCnano UPLC in DDA mode using an 88‑min method with a linear gradient of 4 %–32 % ACN/0.1 % FA over 90 min at 300 nL/min flow; total cycle time is 120 min per fraction. For TMT‑labeled samples, first fractionate pooled peptides by high‑pH reversed‑phase chromatography.

steps.title: Search MS data with Proteome Discoverer
steps.instruction: Search raw data using Proteome Discoverer 2.4 with the Sequest HT engine against the reviewed Homo sapiens UniProt database; use the parameters in Table 2 (variable mods: deamidated (N,Q), oxidation (M), acetylation (protein N‑terminus), biotinylation (Y; C₁₈H₂₃N₃O₃S); fixed mod: carbamidomethyl (C); max missed cleavages = 2; precursor tolerance = 20 ppm; fragment tolerance = 0.5 Da; peptide FDR = 0.01).

steps.title: Statistical analysis in Perseus
steps.instruction: Analyze the identified proteins in Perseus: transform LFQ values to log₂, median‑normalize, impute missing values with random numbers drawn from a normal distribution shifted down 1.8 SD and with a width of 0.3, perform Student’s t‑test comparing BAR samples to negative controls, and set a cutoff for high‑confidence proximal proteins (optional ROC‑based analysis).
